cells.tense: You're tending what's growing between people, and you're doing it right now, not someday.
cells.ask: Tell one person, out loud, what you made possible between you. Don't ask for anything back this time.
cells.core:
You're doing it now, and you know you're doing it. Someone says something true in your company they couldn't say alone, and some of that is you — the way you stayed steady while it came out. You're not managing anyone. You're keeping the room warm enough for what's real to show up in it.

The risk is that tending this smoothly stops being seen, by them and by you. It's working, and working isn't the same as known. You don't need credit. But you do need the thing to have a witness, or you'll keep giving away something you could be sharing. Say what you made possible, once, plainly, and let the two of you have the fact of it instead of only the benefit.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping the room warm. Say so, once, out loud.
cells.verb: holding the space where feeling between people can move and settle
cells.place: the garden where what's still small gets tended without being pulled at

cells.tense: You're bracing for the moment something you're tending will need you, and you're already there in advance.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're tending have a bad day without stepping in. Watch what it does on its own.
cells.core:
You're ahead of everything, already tending what hasn't gone wrong yet. Someone's mood, a silence, a text that's a little slower coming back — you're inside all of it before it arrives, working to keep it from tipping. From where you're standing it feels like care. From the outside it looks like bracing.

Here's the cost. Things that grow do some of it in conditions you'd rather control, and when you can't, you take the whole forecast on yourself and call it protection. What you're doing is real. It's running past the point where it helps. Set one thing down — something you're holding that isn't asking to be held — and find out what it is when your hands aren't on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for a future the thing itself hasn't chosen yet.

cells.place: the garden where what's still small gets tended without being pulled at

cells.tense: You cared about what was growing, and you're still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're tending, to a person you trust, as plainly as you can. No story about why.
cells.core:
You're not cold. You're just further back than you used to be, and the distance is doing its old reliable job of preventing more of the same. Feeling your way toward people again is more than you have right now, and forcing it would only hollow you out.

What's gone missing isn't the ability. It's the plain seeing of what's in front of you — who's actually here, what this thing actually needs. Getting it back is small and unspectacular: look at one thing you're tending and say what you see, out loud, in words you'd use for your own life. That'll do more than feeling your way back to it.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's growing. Say what you see out loud.

cells.tense: You tend the space between people every day and you've been calling it their doing instead.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been doing for the room and claim it once — 'I'm doing this' — no taking it back.
cells.core:
It's already happening. People leave your company standing up straighter and you call it the good energy of the group, the timing, good chemistry — as if the warmth between people ran by itself. It doesn't. You're the one holding one end of it, and you, of all people, haven't been told.

That's what's out of place. You're acting right there, running steady, and your word for it is missing. What's happening between the two of you is partly your work, and you've been giving the credit to the room. Say it once, to yourself or out loud to someone: this is mine. You don't have to make it a big thing. You just have to stop being the only one who doesn't know it's you.
cells.sheetLine: The warmth in the room is partly your doing. Own the doing.

attempts.check: The record doesn't say the person actually does the tending — only that the capacity is available. The reader could reasonably say 'I'm the one who keeps things going for everyone else, I don't need the same back.' The ask survives being wrong: telling someone the truth plainly once is useful whether or not my read is accurate. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'You're holding space for everyone's feelings' — that's a picture the record doesn't support, and it would flatter the card instead of the person.
